resources.string: LinkGuard
LinkGuard checks links before they open

When you tap a link in WhatsApp, Telegram or SMS, LinkGuard checks it first. Safe links open straight away in your browser. If a link looks like a scam, you will see a warning, and you can still choose to open it.
LinkGuard never saves or sends the links you open. No account needed.
your browser

LinkGuard is not a browser

LinkGuard never shows web pages. It checks each link in a split second and then opens it in %1$s, the browser you already use. Your bookmarks, history, saved passwords and tabs stay exactly as they are.
Android will call LinkGuard your “browser app”. That is only so LinkGuard can see links first. Every link still opens in %1$s.

Apps like Telegram, Instagram, Facebook and LinkedIn often open links inside the app, where LinkGuard can’t check them. To stay safe from scam links, turn off the in-app browser in that app’s settings (in Telegram: Settings → Chat Settings → In-app browser), or tap ⋮ and choose “Open in browser”.

How LinkGuard works
Why you need it, and how it decides which links to warn about.
Why it’s needed

Scam messages on WhatsApp and SMS often carry links that look real: a fake bank page, a “KYC update” form or an app that steals money. One tap is enough to cause harm, and a fake web address can be hard to spot.
Where LinkGuard sits
LinkGuard sits between the link you tap and your browser. It checks the link in a split second, then opens it in %1$s. It never shows web pages itself.
Safe links open straight away
Well-known websites and official ones, such as government (.gov.in) and bank websites, open immediately. If a link looks fine, you see nothing at all.
Spotting scam links

LinkGuard looks for the tricks scammers use: websites pretending to be a bank or a well-known brand, app downloads from outside the Play Store, hidden payment requests, brand-new websites and unusual web addresses. It also checks a list of tens of thousands of known scam and harmful websites, collected from leading international security databases and updated every day.
Reports from other users
When several LinkGuard users report the same website as a scam, others are warned to be careful.
You always decide
LinkGuard never blocks a link. Every warning explains the problem in simple words and offers “Open anyway”. LinkGuard never saves the links you open.
